rv.q: Even in a concert staging, the momentum starts high and gets higher.
It's flesh and blood shaped by discipline and artistry into a parade of vital, pulsing talent.
Chicago - the best musical in London since the National'
Under Leigh Silverman's direction, the cast craftily exploits every comic opportunity, and smoothly inhabits David Korins'
Bebe Neuwirth is sensational as Velma, a sister convict Roxie shoves out of the spotlight.
It remains a heartening experience, a life-affirming dedication to the magic and art of theatre, and something that absolutely should not be missed.
If anything can revitalise the moribund West End and restore a jaded theatregoer's faith in the form, this is it.
What seemed cynical in 1975 is now au courant.

I am typically of the opinion that no show has any business occupying a Broadway house for more than a decade: Theater is ephemeral, and the magic tends to wear off as the years pass and performances become stale. ’Chicago’ makes this a difficult position to maintain. Ten thousand performances later, it's still dazzling.
For a Broadway musical that has lasted thousands of performances, 'Chicago' is in remarkably good shape.

cn.t: Critics praise this stripped-down revival as sharp, sassy, and wildly entertaining, with Kander and Ebb's score and Fosse-style choreography remaining potent after decades. The show defies expectations by staying vital and energetic.

ru.inst: On sale when the box office opens on a first-come, first-served basis. 25 tickets available. Cash and credit card. Limit 2.

so.inst: Available at the box office on the day of the performance only if the show is sold out. Standing positions at the back of the orchestra. Limit 2.

sg.vl: Center Orchestra D-J — Best In House
sg.ra: Ambassador's diagonal lot creates a 44'11" proscenium on a hexagonal floor; Center Orchestra D-J is the only zone where Krapp's wide stage reads straight-on with no side-angle skew. Seats 105-109 center the thrust for Chicago's on-stage band riser.

sg.vl: Front Mezz A-B 100-128 — Aerial Sweet Spot
sg.ra: Because Krapp tilted the house diagonally to squeeze 1,125 seats onto a 100x100 lot, the Front Mezz sits unusually close to the stage with a steep rake — Row A delivers a Bob Fosse aerial-choreography view Orchestra can't match, for less than Center Orch premium.

sg.vl: Rear Mezz A-B Center — Budget Panorama
sg.ra: Ambassador's hexagonal diagonal geometry means Rear Mezz isn't pushed as far back as standard proscenium houses — decent rake clears heads, and the 250-seat rear balcony is built into the same structure as the Front Mezz (no secondary overhang).

This is the exact section the diagonal orientation penalizes: Krapp's 44'11" wide stage sits at an angle to the house, so outer seats (13-30 per NYTix) look diagonally across the proscenium rather than into it — Chicago's thrust-edge numbers become extreme raking angles.
